[Triton] Preserve volatile loads in select combining (#11240)

A regular unused load can be removed, but a volatile load must remain.
As a result, the old code produced two volatile reads instead of one and
returned the value from the second read.

[Tutorial] Fix FP8 attention V descriptor offsets (#11461)

## Summary

The FP8 attention path stores V physically as `[Z, H, HEAD_DIM, N_CTX]`,
but the tutorial described it as `[HEAD_DIM, Z * H * N_CTX]`. That
flattening crosses non-contiguous logical dimensions, so descriptor
loads for every batch/head after the first read the wrong values.

This change describes the same storage as `[Z * H * HEAD_DIM, N_CTX]`
and starts each V tile at row `off_hz * HEAD_DIM`. The layout now
matches the physical tensor for both host and device descriptor paths.

A focused regression test compares the Triton output against a reference
computed from the quantized FP8 inputs with multiple batches and heads.

Fixes #11440.

## Validation

- On the original code, the new test fails with 1,857 / 32,768
mismatched elements and a maximum absolute error of 0.4307.
- On the patched code, the regression test and 16 existing FP8 forward
configurations pass.
- A separate matrix covering both descriptor paths, causal and
non-causal attention, head dimensions 64 and 128, and sequence lengths
128 through 1024 passes on an RTX 5090.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passes.

[PROTON] Release HIP metric buffers before runtime teardown (#11824)

PR description written by Codex

HIP graph metric buffers can survive until after HIP teardown and abort
process exit in `hipFreeHost`, even after `proton.finalize()`. Call
`hipInit(0)` before registering Proton's existing shutdown handler, then
release the buffers in the SDK tool finalizer after its tracing and
PC-sampling buffer flushes. Keep the buffers across ordinary session
finalization so captured graphs remain replayable.

The production diff covers ROCprofiler lifecycle handling and a dynamic
HIP initialization wrapper. Tests cover single and sequential sessions,
replay after finalize, exit without explicit finalize, and profiling
started before Torch/HIP initialization. Native Proton passed all 16
focused tests, seven lifecycle probes, and ten repeated early-start
cases on MI355X with ROCm 7.2.3 and SDK 1.3.5, using the existing
compiler and Torch binaries. Omitting startup HIP initialization
reproduces both early-start exit aborts.

[AMD][gfx950][Gluon] Add cd_regclass to mfma and mfma_scaled (#11792)

`gl.amd.cdna3.mfma` and `gl.amd.cdna4.mfma_scaled` take an optional
`cd_regclass`: "a" to keep the MFMA accumulator (C and D) in AGPRs, "v"
to keep it in VGPRs. It is recorded as `amdg.cd_regclass` on `tt.dot` /
`tt.dot_scaled`, and the MFMA lowering wraps each tile's accumulator in
an empty inline asm with a tied "=a,0" / "=v,0" constraint, right before
the tile's first MFMA and right after its last. This gives a kernel
per-call control over the MFMA form without process-wide LLVM options.

[GPU] Count small histograms with warp ballots (#11820)

Add a new ballot-based histogram
```
Generic:
  zero shared bins → atomic increment per input → read bins

Ballot:
  computeWarpHistogram (ballot + popcount) → reduceWarpHistograms → distributeHistogram
``` 

We heuristically choose ballot based on benchmarks for
```
!hasCrossCTAScratch(op) && bins * warps <= 4 && (bins <= 2 || N <= 128)
```

GB300 measurements across 13 configurations showed lower latency as:
**4.5–6.2% for two bins** and **1.3–3.9% for four bins**, with no

Preserve source locations for Python 3.13 inspection (#11801)

Python 3.13 uses precise definition locations when `inspect` retrieves
source. Triton's `specialize` and `aggregate` wrappers preserve the
original file or class identity but keep a generated location. As a
result, `inspect.getsource` can return only a signature fragment for a
specialized function or raise `OSError: source code not available` for
an aggregate class.

Preserve the original Python function and class definition locations.
The adjusted JIT source-location fields stay as they are, and the class
location is copied only when the original class provides it.

## Validation

- CPU source-inspection probes reproduced both failures on Python
3.13.15 and passed with this patch. Python 3.12.13 behavior was
unchanged.
- The specialization probe preserved generated source, JIT location
metadata, and the cache key. The aggregate probes covered module-level
and nested classes and preserved observed metadata, hash inputs, and
value construction.
- Both affected files at upstream base
`38e38e7dc33822d0446e2db4c4024a2bf6929668` match the source used for
validation. Downstream Python 3.13 compatibility CI passed the relevant
unquarantined checks using the identical source changes.
- Pre-commit passed for the exact base-to-head diff, including Ruff,
YAPF, and mypy.

- [x] The description explains the problem and why the change is needed.
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --from-ref
38e38e7dc33822d0446e2db4c4024a2bf6929668 --to-ref HEAD`, using the exact
upstream base and a writable Go cache.
- [x] This PR does not add repository tests because downstream Python
3.13 CI exercises the affected paths; the local baseline/candidate
probes above verify the specific source-inspection behavior.
- [x] I have not added any `lit` tests.

Fix register allocation for padded warp groups (#11287)

## Summary

- Clamp per-partition register allocations to NVVM's minimum of 24
registers.
- Reuse the same minimum for the default warp group.
- Add an end-to-end regression test from warp-group allocation through
NVIDIA lowering.

## Problem

`AllocateWarpGroups::padToMaxWarpGroups` pads smaller
`ttg.warp_specialize` operations to the largest worker footprint in the
module. Those synthetic no-op partitions request 16 registers. The
allocator could copy that value into `actualRegisters`, so
`ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM` generated `nvvm.setmaxregister ... 16`.
NVVM only accepts register targets from 24 through 256.

A valid source-level kernel with sequential handoffs using different
worker-warp counts can therefore fail during compilation.

## Fix

Clamp each partition estimate to 24 before computing warp-group budgets.
This both keeps the lowered `nvvm.setmaxregister` legal and accounts for
the padding warp group's real register consumption when distributing the
remaining budget to the default warp group.

## Validation

- New allocation-only regression check.
- New allocation-to-NVVM lowering regression check.
- Existing `allocate_warp_groups.mlir` checks in normal and instrumented
modes.
- Existing NVIDIA `warp_specialize_to_llvm.mlir` checks.
- Source-level Gluon reproducer compiled to PTX and cubin and launched
on B200.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`.

[Build] Honor artifact mirrors for AMD codegen downloads (#11850)

AMD bootstrap LLVM and prebuilt AMD codegen downloads construct public
blob-storage URLs directly, so wheel builds cannot download them when
their network requires the artifact mirror configured by
`OAIARTIFACTS_BASE_URL`.

Route both downloads through the existing `DependencyArchive` mirror
selection. The bootstrap download keeps its independently pinned LLVM
revision, build number, and checksum. Public downloads remain the
default when no mirror is configured.

Validation:
- Added six regression cases in the existing build tests, covering both
artifacts with no mirror, a mirror, and a mirror with a trailing slash.
They exercise download URL selection, checksum verification, extraction,
and copying with generated archives.
- On a Brix CPU devbox, the original implementation failed all four
mirror cases and passed the two public cases; the fix passed all six.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed.
